# Warbler issue 38 - Pellam Marsh walk

Highlight: a least bittern, almost hidden in the cattails. Odalys pointed it out with two words, "stand still", and it stepped out into view.

How to find your chainring bolt circle diameter

Before you buy a new chainring, you need to know your bolt circle diameter (BCD). It is the distance across the circle that goes through the center of all the bolts. To measure it, take a ruler and measure from the center of one bolt hole to the center of the hole opposite, if there is an even number of bolts. For five bolts, measure from one bolt to the far side of the two opposite bolts.

Common sizes are 110, 130 and 144 mm. If you are not sure, send us a photo with a ruler in view and we will help.

Don't feel bad, first-year birders mix up the two. The Cooper's has a rounded tail tip and a big head that sticks out front. Sharp-shinned looks like a flying cross with a small head. Take photos of the tail, it saves you every time.

How to check your tire pressure

Use a floor pump with a gauge. Check the pressure before every ride, because tires lose a little air each day. The correct range is printed on the sidewall of the tire. Wide tires need less pressure, narrow tires need more.

A tip from our workshop: after rain, drop the pressure a little for more grip on the wet road.

How to fit a new cassette

You need a chain whip, a cassette lockring tool and a wrench. Remove the wheel, then take off the quick-release skewer. Hold the cassette with the chain whip and turn the lockring tool counterclockwise. Slide the old cassette off and the new one on, making sure the splines line up. Tighten the lockring until it clicks.

If the wheel has a thru-axle, the steps are the same, but check the manual for the torque value.

How to know if your brake pads are worn

Look at the pad from the side. If the friction material is thinner than 1.5 mm, replace it. You may also hear a squeal or a grinding sound, or feel the lever pull closer to the bar. Always replace pads in pairs, both on the same wheel.

How to clean and oil your chain

Wipe the chain with a rag. Apply a thin line of oil on each link and turn the pedals backward for a minute. Wipe off the extra oil, because oil that stays on the outside collects dirt. A clean chain lasts twice as long.
